name: Paraswap Augustus V6 uniswapV3SwapCallback missing caller check
date_note: DeFiHackLabs / press say 2024-03-20 (when Paraswap paused V6); the first on-chain abuse is 2024-03-19 18:25:35 UTC.
verdict_reason: Yoink tx 0x35a73969... (block 19470561, index 0, 2024-03-19 18:25:35 UTC) is the FIRST call to Augustus V6 uniswapV3SwapCallback (0xfa461e33) that has no Augustus swap above it, in all of blocks 19426044-19482000 (trace_filter, toAddress=Augustus; code first present at 19426044 = 2024-03-13 12:06 UTC; ~56,000 blocks, 2024-03-13 to 2024-03-21). The next such call is 11 h 13 min later (block 19473885, 2024-03-20 05:38:47). No attacker tx, pending or reverted, precedes or shares the block; no direct 0xfa461e33 tx to Augustus is in the 2024-03-19 mempool-dumpster; Yoink's tx is private. So there is no hacker to front-run: Yoink was the first exploiter (it pulled 12,479 OPSEC from one approving wallet 0x0cc396f5 and sold it for 6.46 WETH; paid 99.8% to the builder, then got 4.34 ETH back from the builder). Returns (corrected 2026-10-21): after Paraswap's on-chain message (block 19507521, 2024-03-24T23:00:59Z) Yoink sent 4.342 ETH to the Safe Paraswap named (0x66E90d840D7C4F3473E25dD8ca361747058c6Db0) in tx 0xa1b1ea5033611603f6e8e5ce5d566ad6b9ad1cd69476e37091c0d90c56c04f90 (block 19508275, 2024-03-25T01:33:35Z): 67.2% of the 6.4633 ETH sale, 99.8% of the bot tx's 4.3499 ETH net. Paraswap asked for the remaining ~2.12 ETH and a 10% bounty split; Yoink declined (2.22 ETH went to the validator); no further transfer found to 2024-05-24. The 'whitehat' label (DeFiHackLabs header, Etherscan) is still not supported by the sequence of events: Yoink was the first exploiter and returned its net profit only after being contacted. Later actors (11 h+) are independent, using the same bug with other victims; they did not replay Yoink's calldata. Unknown != none for private txs.

bots.replay_evidence: bot analysis decode (decode_script.py ok=True) of tx0: x=0, [CALL Augustus V6 0x00000000fdac7708....0xfa461e33 len 388] [UNWRAP]. The 388-byte call is Augustus V6 selector 0xfa461e33 (the uniswapV3SwapCallback entry per the Velora/Neptune write-ups) made by the Yoink contract itself; its data words name the victim wallet 0x0cc396f5 (word 5) and the OPSEC and WETH tokens (words 9-10); the trace shows Augustus calling V3 pool 0x45f4d604 swap(recipient = Yoink contract); the pool pays 6.4633 WETH to Yoink and, in its callback into Augustus, Augustus pulls 12,479.437 OPSEC from the victim wallet to the pool (OPSEC.transferFrom). Words are in incidents/paraswap-2024/callback_calldata_words.json beside the two later actors' callback words for comparison: same selector/layout, different victim/token/amount - evidence the bug was being used independently, NOT a replay of an earlier hack tx (none exists). tx1 (index 1, value 914): wrap 2.0102 ETH, buy OPSEC from V3 pool 0x45f4d604 (callback pays), sell on V2 pool 0x515d4595, unwrap 2.1174 ETH, coinbase 0.0980 ETH: post-exploit arbitrage of the price Yoink's tx0 had just moved, i.e. related-not-frontrun.
bots.notes: Builder is Yoink-affiliated per research/bot-re (pubkey 0x81476ce9..., label "I can haz block?"): same pubkey as the Ronin builder. Builder refund (index 13) is the same mechanism documented at Ronin.

headline_text: Yoink was the first to exploit Paraswap Augustus V6's missing callback caller check, pulling 12,479 OPSEC (6.46 WETH) from one approving wallet 11 hours before anyone else; after Paraswap's on-chain message it sent 4.342 ETH (99.8% of its 4.35 ETH net, 67% of the 6.46 ETH sale) to the Safe Paraswap named, and declined to send the rest.
